remaining_gaps: No citable end source in the packet. The order suspends the Eight-Hour Law provisions for the duration of the national emergency proclaimed by Proclamation 2914; that emergency does not end by its own terms within the order's life. The end that applies is statutory: sections 203 and 204 of Pub. L. 87-581 (76 Stat. 357, approved Aug. 13, 1962, effective sixty days after enactment) repealed sections 1 and 2 of the Act of Aug. 1, 1892 as amended Mar. 3, 1913, the provisions this order suspended, with a continuing proviso for contracts existing on the effective date. That statute is held only as an unregistered source-ladder text (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/opus-refetch_https_www.govinfo.gov_content_pkg_STATUTE-76_pdf_STATUTE-76-Pg357.pdf_a0da22ffea.txt) and the dossier's citable later-event list for this order is empty. A source supplement registering that text is required; the registered clause span also needs an inventory correction because it begins in front-matter of the Federal Register issue.

The order vests the Secretary of the Navy's interest in and control over moneys deposited in a Treasury suspense account under EO 10426 in the Secretary of the Interior hereafter, with the moneys to be expended or deposited as the Submerged Lands Act and the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act provide. A performed-on-issuance reading is not supported: the held 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_10525.txt) reproduces the order among the texts that still had general effect on January 20, 1989, and no held source shows the suspense-account moneys were exhausted or the transfer revoked or superseded afterwards. Needed: a source after 1989 (or a statute or order) showing how the vesting ended. The dossier also notes that its current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256.

EO 10700 (signed 1957-02-25, held and citable as actor text) section 6 supersedes EO 10483 and the provisions amendatory of it contained in other Executive orders, which reaches this amendment, but its section 7 makes that effective on July 1, 1957 unless funds appropriated for the National Security Council were not then available for the Board, in which case on the later date they became available. No held source shows whether the funds were available on July 1, 1957, so no exact first-end date can be recorded. EO 10700 was later amended (by EO 10773 of July 1, 1958 and EO 10838) and revoked by EO 10920, whose text is held but not citable from this packet. Needed: a held source for the availability of the National Security Council funds, or another dated source for the effective date of EO 10700.
